title: WhatsApp Pay and UPI AutoPay: Where to Cancel (2026)
metaDescription: WhatsApp's payment pages do not describe UPI AutoPay mandates. Learn where to look, cancel with the merchant, and revoke in the UPI app that approved it.
h1: Can you cancel a UPI AutoPay mandate from WhatsApp Pay?
summary: WhatsApp Pay sends money and pays bills over UPI, but WhatsApp's India payments page and terms do not describe creating, pausing or cancelling UPI AutoPay mandates. I could not confirm any WhatsApp screen for managing mandates, so for a recurring debit, cancel with the merchant first, then find the mandate in the UPI app or bank where it was approved and revoke it there with your UPI PIN.
stepsHeading: How to stop a UPI AutoPay debit linked to WhatsApp Pay

steps.name: Cancel with the merchant
steps.text: Cancel the subscription on the merchant's website or app and save the confirmation. HDFC Bank advises doing this first, so the merchant stops starting new charges.

steps.name: Look in WhatsApp's payments settings
steps.text: Open WhatsApp payments settings. WhatsApp's payments page says past transactions can be viewed there. I could not confirm a list of AutoPay mandates in that screen, so if none appears, move on to the next step.

steps.name: Check the UPI apps and bank you use
steps.text: Open each UPI app you have used and go to Profile or Settings, then AutoPay, Mandates or Subscriptions. In Google Pay, tap your profile picture and select Autopay.

steps.name: Cancel or revoke with your UPI PIN
steps.text: Select the active mandate, choose Cancel or Revoke, and enter your UPI PIN. In Google Pay, open the Live tab, tap the mandate and choose Cancel autopay.

steps.name: Confirm the status changed
steps.text: Check that the mandate shows as cancelled or revoked. Keep a screenshot of the status and the confirmation, then check your bank statement after the next due date.

sections.heading: What WhatsApp's official pages cover
paragraphs: WhatsApp's payments page says the feature is powered by BHIM UPI and processed by payment partners in India, with money moving directly between bank accounts. Its terms describe payments made through payment service providers over UPI, and bill payments made through BBPS.

Neither the payments page nor the India payments terms that I read mention UPI AutoPay, e-mandates or subscription debits, and my searches found no WhatsApp-specific mandate guide. Treat any claim that WhatsApp manages AutoPay as unconfirmed until WhatsApp publishes it.

sections.heading: Finding the app that holds the mandate
paragraphs: A UPI mandate is changed in the app or bank where it was approved. HDFC Bank says mandates are visible in the UPI app where they were authorised, so the first app you open may not show it, and a WhatsApp payment does not guarantee the mandate sits in WhatsApp.
Keep any pre-debit SMS or notification. It usually names the merchant, amount, debit date and mandate reference, which tells you which app or bank to search.

sections.heading: Cancelling, and what happens next
paragraphs: Cancelling a mandate stops future debits, but a payment that has already completed is not reversed, according to HDFC Bank's guide. A debit that started before you cancelled can still finish, so check your statement for several days afterwards.

WhatsApp's terms say that once you submit a payment through a payment service provider it is final, and WhatsApp cannot provide refunds or chargebacks in its capacity as a third-party app provider. The terms name WhatsApp as the first point of contact for UPI complaints, then the PSP bank, your bank and NPCI, in that order.

sections.heading: Common problems
paragraphs: A loan or debt collection mandate usually cannot be cancelled through the UPI app. HDFC Bank says those must be cancelled with the merchant. If Google Pay returns an error on a cancel, the linked bank account must be active, so reactivate it first.
Deleting WhatsApp is not a way to cancel a mandate, and I found nothing suggesting it changes one. Check the status in the UPI app or bank afterwards.

sections.heading: Where Essara fits in
paragraphs: Essara works from a list you keep yourself. You add each subscription or mandate with its amount, billing cycle and next renewal date, and see the upcoming auto-debits in one place. It does not connect to WhatsApp, your UPI app, your bank or your SMS, so the entries are only as current as the ones you type in.

faqs.q: Can I cancel UPI AutoPay from WhatsApp?
faqs.a: Not confirmed. WhatsApp's India payments page and terms describe sending money and bill payments, and do not mention UPI AutoPay mandates. If a mandate appears in WhatsApp's payments settings, cancel it there. Otherwise, revoke it in the UPI app or bank where it was approved.

faqs.q: Does deleting WhatsApp stop a UPI AutoPay debit?
faqs.a: I found no evidence that it does, so do not rely on it. Revoke the mandate in the app where it was approved, then check that its status shows as cancelled or revoked.

faqs.q: Will WhatsApp refund a payment I did not want?
faqs.a: WhatsApp's terms say a payment is final once submitted through a payment service provider, and that WhatsApp cannot provide refunds or chargebacks as a third-party app provider. For a disputed debit, the terms make WhatsApp the first contact for UPI complaints, with escalation to the PSP bank, your bank and NPCI after that.

faqs.q: Why did a debit come through after I cancelled?
faqs.a: A payment that had already started can still complete, and a merchant may keep trying if the mandate is active in another app. Check every UPI app and your bank for the mandate, and send the merchant your cancellation confirmation with the debit details.
